notes.title: [1.5] The End
notes.content:
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/9781553/8a2baec3da1295ac7adbfb7e66ae33a3708f8a82.gif
Hey all,

Today I am releasing the 1.5 update. This will be the final update for Shoppy Mart: Steam Edition. I have been debating when I was going to officially close this chapter of my life, and I think it is time.

Here is the changelog for the final update:

Permanent price reduction from $4.99 USD to $1.99 USD as there will be no further updates to the game. 
Made it so that the seasonal events will activate automatically as opposed to me uploading a new build manually. The Halloween Event will run from October 1st to October 31st, and the Christmas Event will run from December 1st to December 31st. These, as always, can be activated from the options menu using the cheatcode "spooky" and "christmas".
I've updated the demo of the game to be more accurate to the state the game is in now. The demo was riddled with bugs that have long been fixed in the full version of the game. Those all have now been fixed and is in a much better state then it was before. 
Fixed a bug where if a coupon was placed off screen if would not allow you to continue, forcing you to restart the game or exit to the main menu. 
Fixed the audio levels on a handful of sound effects and music to make it all around a better experience. 
Fixed a bug where the resolution would change when you would start a new game.

I want to thank you all for the continued support for Shoppy Mart, I am continually surprised by how many people continue to purchase and play this little game I started working on almost 4 years ago now. I'd like to take this moment to take you through some of the development of the game, along with some features that never made it into the game, such as a big update I was working on, Shoppe Mart: Fantasy Edition. 
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/9781553/27a390980f99794817854a7612d186ed97009a5b.png

Shoppy Mart was the first game I ever made. On a whim I uploaded it to itch.io and to my surprise, people started downloading it, asking questions about it, and bringing recommendations to me about the game. Back then it looked like this:
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/9781553/9a43fa61e3e9bf31ccc1d2521097b66c71e8d2ae.gif
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/9781553/6375b1fcb56ec6c61dfb1a509ec1616900a0d7e0.gif

From itch.io I got requests to put the game on Steam Greenlight, so I put it on Steam Greenlight, then the game got voted through Steam Greenlight and now I had to make a real game!!

It was scary, and new, and I definitely felt that I was under-qualified to be doing such a thing, but I did it, and although the review score right now is sitting at 63%, it still performed better then I could have ever imagined.

I had a lot of doubts about making a game about being a grocery store clerk. I had decided to make a grocery store clerk simulator after I had worked at a grocery store for two years and thought that my coworkers and I were treated... not super well, and wanted to allow people to see what it is like on the other side of it. There are some people who understood what I was going for, and I am glad that Shoppy Mart could give them (to the best of my abilities at the time) the experience of being a grocery store clerk. 

There were a handful of ideas that I had started implementing but then never left it in the game. The original idea is that you would eventually be able to manage the whole store, but this was my first game, and I had no idea how to do the ideas I had for the game. Some of the ideas that I worked on that never made it into the final game were:

Stocking items in the store.
Manging the schedule for other employees once you got promoted to shift manager.
Check out speed competitions
Express Lane
Talking to other employees in the break room.
Managing your money to take care of your car, apartment, food, gas, ect.
Going to the bar to drink/talk to other people.
The back story of the dark history of the company that would be revealed throughout the game.
Selling alcohol and having to check IDs.
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/9781553/fc70ceab690d4191506b1a53134b2af5a5e23c5f.gif

Checking your phone and using different apps while inbetween customers.
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/9781553/2c1e2a66ae070c7e3dcf9c73746f5e96e7debdbd.gif
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/9781553/87ff0aee74e161dc44da0e29c26737ca50c3fb9d.gif

I also started work on a character named Skele Bones who is a checker who has been working at Shoppy Mart for forever. I ended up abandoning it as I never figured out a good way to connect his story in the main game. I abandoned his solo game later on, but you can play a part of it on itch.io.
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/9781553/251acda9ce86335f9b7fc864a4d623b5c08f91f4.gif

Shoppe Mart: Fantasy Edition, was a huge update I was working on that would completely change the game. You were now a loyal merchant of The Shoppe Mart Kingdom, responsible for trading with other kingdoms, such as The Dairy Isle and The Frozen Isles in order to keep the kingdom running smoothly. It was ambitous and fun to work on, but in the end I didn't feel like it made enough sense to continue development on it. It was so different that it should almost be an entirely different game. There was going to be wizards, goblins, elves, ect. Maybe one day I'll be able to make that kind of game, and maybe it was wrong of me to cancel it, but that's just part of being a 'in my free time' game developer. I work a full time job and don't have the time to pursue every idea I have. Here are two gifs of what the Fantasy Update looked like, along with an early prototype of the trading. 
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/9781553/b4de809c23f028372a4204b3d69e06e5293139ea.gif
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/9781553/a8b7873a70ceec41a436114b5bdc0f9302e15b4f.gif
There was many more, but those are some of the more interesting ones. 


Some of the stats from Shoppy Mart: Steam Edition:

Shoppy Mart has been downloaded/purchased nearly 100,000 times in total.
Shoppy Mart has been viewed on Youtube 7,000,000+ times total.
 2.5% of all players on Steam have beaten the game. [spoiler](and reached hell.)[/spoiler]
Buttface was the most popular choice for customer unlocks.
It took 13 months for the secret file to be found and the symbols in the handbook to be decoded, which revealed some cheat codes in the game.

As for what is next, I am continuing to make games in my free time and am planning to make a sequel to SM using the experience and skills I have gained in the 4 years since I first started working on SM. I want the sequel to be much more of a 'fun' video game then SM was. I think it does a solid enough job of being a grocery store clerk simulator, but it definitely can be boring, much like the job can be in real life. This is what I was aiming for when I originally started making the game, but I took that idea a little too seriously and should have tried to make the game more engaging and rewarding as a player. I want SM2 to be everything I wanted SM to be, but couldn't be, because I lacked the experience, programming skills, project management skills, time management skills, and game development lessons that I have learned now. 

I want to thank you all for the lessons you've taught me, the patience you've shown, and the support you have given me on this journey as I continue to learn how to become a 'real' game developer.

You can follow me and my future endeavors on Twitter and on itch.io.
https://twitter.com/pezomi
https://pezomi.itch.io/

Thank You.

-Brady

notes.title: [FIX] Black Screen on Startup
notes.content:
Hey guys, 

For those of those who have the black screen on startup issue I believe I have found a solution for those of you affected. I actually found the solution in a Hyper Light Drifter steam community discussion, some users were having similar problems in Hyper Light Drifter and it should fix the problem for you guys as well. 

Hyper Light Drifter is a game that was also made in GameMaker: Studio and this solution has helped people having the same problem with Shoppy Mart. 

Now here's the important part of the post:


1. options.ini tweaks:
Open options.ini located in your game's install directory and change "CreateTexturesOnDemand=0" to "CreateTexturesOnDemand=1"
You can also try changing "AlternateSyncMethod=1" to "AlternateSyncMethod=0"
2. Make sure graphics drivers are up to date
3. Disable any anti-virus software you have running
4. If you are on a laptop with integrated/discrete combo make sure the discrete card is used
5. Post your system information (Steam->Help->System Information)


Here's the link to the full post: https://steamcommunity.com/app/257850/discussions/0/365163686044734763/

I've posted this as a response in threads a while ago, but I figured an offical announcement might help if anyone else is having issues.

Thanks,
Brady

notes.title: 1.3.2 - Crash on Startup + Achievement Bug Fixes
notes.content:
The two major bug fixes this patch are:

Crash on Startup:
The root of this issue was with GameMaker: Studio, in one of its updates it caused an issue with GameMaker and how it communicates with the Steam API. I hadn't thought that the reason for the crashes would have actually been on GameMaker's end. Hopefully this also fixes the black screens on startup. If it doesn't, let me know and I'll continue to look into it. 


Achievements:
The root of this issue was a mixup between GameMaker: Studio and myself, for the since the Feburary Update, the only way your stats would update would be if you were to open and close the In-Game Steam Menu (Shift + Tab). That was why some people were having issues and other weren't. If at any time you were to Shift+Tab and then return to the game, it would start counting the stats, if you never opened up that menu and scanned 1,000,000 items, none of them would have counted. 

Both of these bugs, to the best of my knowledge, have now been fixed, sorry about any inconenience that these issues may have caused.

There are some really minor bug fixes in here too:
Some typo fixes, audio tweaks, and experience system tweaks.

Thanks for the continued support,
-Brady

It's Christmas Time at Shoppy Mart and everyone is in the Christmas spirit! All the customers are dressed in their winter gear and need groceries!

25 new customers in Christmas attire!
6 new seasonal produce items!
All new Christmas themed menus/backgrounds!
50+ new dialogue responses!
Update to a couple pages in the Handbook

You can now move between the 2 produce pages with the left and right arrow while you're holding shift, per request.


I hope you enjoy it! Merry Christmas!
-Brady

notes.title: Patch 1.1.2 - The Bag Patch
notes.content:
http://i.imgur.com/w3jeHZC.gif
The community has made it clear that something about the bagging system needs to be changed, so I changed it! 

Here's whats new:

Items in grocrey bags can now be moved around,
The grocery bag can now be looked into by LEFT clicking on it, and closed by RIGHT clicking the bag.
The register now displays the weight of an item when it is scanned.


Later this week I'll be updating the handbook with the new information.

Hopefully this fixes most of the frustrations with the bagging system.

Let me know what you think!
-Brady

notes.title: Patch 1.1.1
notes.content:
Patch 1.1.1 has a handful of bug fixes, a new performance mode for lower end computers, and the end of the Halloween event.

Halloween Event:

The Halloween event is now over! If you ever want to get spooky again, you can type in the cheat code 'spooky' on the options screen.

Also, I noticed I didn't actually have all of the new characters coded in to be selected, so there are 4 new halloween customers! 


Performance Mode:

I've been looking for a solution for how to make the game run better on lower end computers and I hope this is it. 'Performance mode' is basically just a 30fps mode, but I've been testing it on my own low end computer and have had a lot of success with the game not stuttering, running super slow, or crashing. I really hope it helps those of you running on low end systems.

You can find this new option in the options menu.


Bug Fixes:

Fixed a handful of audio bugs that happen when transitioning from the main menu.
Added a bigger 'hitbox' for the club card and coupon when scanning.
Candy from the candy bowl doesn't get stuck on the grocery bag.


I'm trying my hardest to give you guys the best product I possibly can. Thank you for your continuned patience and support!

-Brady

notes.title: Halloween Update: Spooky Mart
notes.content:
http://i.imgur.com/rZsCm9y.png
With Halloween just around the corner, Shoppy Mart has put up all of their spooky decorations and all of their customers are dressing up and getting spooky. Some are even getting *too* spooky...

Here's whats new at Spooky Mart (1.1 Update) :

Shoppy Mart is now 300% more spooky
20 new customers
6 new produce items
You can hand out candy to the customers!
Added a new achivement
Fixed the achievement bug. (hopefully)
Fixed the items scanned stats bug
Optimizations in the object handling for hopefully a smoother experience on low end systems. I'll be continuing to work on this in the following updates.

I apologize in advance for how spooky I have made the game in this update. 

Just in case some people get too spooked, if you type 'spooky' in as a cheat code in the options menu you can toggle the update on and off. That also means that after the event, you can revisit Spooky Mart whenever you want! 

Happy Halloween! 
-Brady

notes.title: 1.0.0 Release!
notes.content:
http://i.imgur.com/wS2MFdn.gif

With Shoppy Mart officially releasing on the 25th, this will be the final update until release! Most everything is the same except (hopefully) all of the bugs are fixed. 

Here's what has been done since last patch:


    Fixed a bug that would skip the ending cutscene.
    Fixed an audio bug that would play the car noise during the work day.
    Fixed a bug where the order would finish if a coupon was still visible.
    Fixed all of the cases I could find of the customers responses not fitting in the chat bubble. 
    Fixed a bug where the handbook wouldn't close if you pushed 'H' to open it and then clicked on a page.
    Fixed the credits bug that would leave a black screen.
    Fixed a bug where if you leveled up twice on day one you wouldn't unlock two customers.


As for what the future holds, I've started working on porting Shoppy Mart over to Android and iOS and have a handful of updates planned for the PC version. 

Here's a photo I took really quick of it working on android:
http://i.imgur.com/EvWvvXV.png

notes.title: Beta 0.0.3 (Pre-Release)
notes.content:
Hey guys, here's the last update until the game releases in a month.

New Stuff:


Changed the tutorial a bit, now you are given a handbook at the end of it that explains the game's mechanics a bit more.
There is a new Handbook icon while checking, so you can look at it if you forget what to do. You can also access it by pushing 'H'.
Added a 'Failed Order Counter'. If you fail an order you'll see a crossed out customer appear in the upper lefthand corner. If you fail 5 orders in the same day you'll get fired.
I lowered the amount of exp required to level up by about 30%.
Added 2 more achievements.
Added the final customer unlock in the game.
The game now has a soft-ending! 
Added the credits to the game.
Fixed the main menu audio bug.
Fixed the 'customer gets stuck on the hand out ads' bug.
Fixed the majority of the customer responses that were not fitting inside the chat bubble. 


You'll probably see some updates over the next couple weeks, if it's anything big I'll make a post about it, if not you can just assume it's some pre-launch bug fixing or polish. Because at this point I'd consider the game about 98% done.

Why 98%?
Because I'll be changing the song that rolls during the credits, and I have to add in the new in-store ads that have been recorded. Also I might be changing around the buttons on the options menu to look a little nicer, but content wise, the game is done! I hope you like it!

-Brady

notes.title: Beta 0.0.2 Update!
notes.content:
The Community Hub is live!

New Stuff:

Added a 'Delete Save File' Button
Easy difficulty exp gain is now halved from the Normal difficulty.
Added a Level 6 Customer Unlock
Added 5 more memos.
Added 10 new achievements.
Added 2 new cheatcodes.
Tweaked the way the game chooses the next customer, so hopefully you'll be seeing all the different types of customers at an even rate.


I'd consider Shoppy Mart about 90% done at this point, with this possibly being the last update to the beta before release. The things left to do are:


Make a soft-ending where the credits roll.
Put in the last couple of customer unlocks.
Finish the tutorial.
Record some new in-store ads. 
Lot's of bug-testing & polishing it up for release!


I moved the release date up 6 days from the original release date of October 1st, to September 25th, mainly because it'll be done sooner then expected, but also because September 25th, 2015 marks one year that I've been working on Shoppy Mart!

That's all for now, Thanks for the continued support! 

-Brady

NOTE: If you're having any issues with the update, I'd recommend deleting your old save file (sorry!) with the new button in the options menu.
